tone_statements.quote: Le mazahua distingue trois tons, deux tons ponctuels : haut (V́) et bas (Ṽ̀) et un ton mélodique bas – haut (V̌). Les voyelles qui portent le ton mélodique se réalisent plus longuement mais la longueur vocalique n’est pas pertinente. La plupart des verbes et des noms sont bisyllabiques. La première syllabe peut avoir un ton ponctuel ou bien un ton mélodique alors que la deuxième syllabe porte uniquement un ton ponctuel.
tone_statements.translation: Mazahua distinguishes three tones, two level tones: high (V́) and low (V̀), and one melodic (contour) low-high tone (V̌). Vowels bearing the melodic tone are realised longer, but vowel length is not distinctive. Most verbs and nouns are bisyllabic. The first syllable may carry a level tone or a melodic tone, whereas the second syllable carries only a level tone.
tone_statements.n_tones: 3 (H, L level + LH rising contour); contour only on the root-initial syllable

tone_statements.translation: In Mazahua two level tones (high and low) and two contour tones (rising and falling) have been identified so far, as specified by Freisinger (1996) and Knapp (2008). sources.note: Instrumental (Praat) study: four lexical tones - two level (alto, bajo) and two contour (ascendente, descendente) - contrastive on the first (stressed) syllable of the bisyllabic radical; F0 and duration ranges per tone (Cuadro 6); the rising tone was missed by Pike 1951/Spotts 1953/Amador 1976; ch. 4 classifies tonal behaviour in compounds into five types (transparent, tonal simplification/dissociation of the unstressed syllable, loss with default unmarked tone, contour-tone shift, lexicalised compounds); ch. 5 relates tone to tonic vs atonic syllables.

sources.note: Second-hand: Ortiz Torres 2023:76 groups 'Knapp (1996)' with the analyses positing a four-tone opposition (haut, bas, descendant-montant, montant-descendant) for Mazahua, adding that none of them gives minimal pairs proving the contrast; Cárdenas & Lastra 2011:13-14 describe it as a systematic study of the Mazahua phonological system (vowels, consonants) based on ample data from Portes Gil and San Miguel Tenochtitlán; precursor of Knapp 2008 (four tones H, L, rising, falling).
